title: Absolute HbA1c–fasting-glucose discrepancy fails to improve transported inflammation prediction: an exploratory two-survey test
abstract: We tested absolute HbA1c-implied-average-glucose minus fasting-glucose discrepancy, |28.7 HbA1c−46.7−FPG|, for incremental prediction of concurrent CRP>3mg/L beyond separate nonlinear glycemic measurements and routine covariates. Weighted logistic models trained in 6,429 NHANES III adults were transported without recalibration to 2,232 NHANES2017–2018 adults. Weighted Brier increased from 0.16634824 to 0.16728829; added-minus-base +0.00094005, approximate fixed-fit target-PSU95% interval [+0.00049573,+0.00132664]. AUC changed by -0.00161584; joint training/target Brier interval [+0.00017524,+0.00190960]. This exploratory negative representation test does not establish new physiology or negate published glycation–inflammation associations. Fasting glucose is not average glucose, and both surveys were historically reused.
